messages:
maria: quick heads-up — several folks hit issues during onboarding the JS SDK. main pain: require vs import, default vs named exports in our docs + examples. also edge runtimes complaining (Cloudflare/Netlify edge). can someone summarize the recommended patterns?

sam: saw one thread where `require('@redwood/sdk')` returned an object with keys under `.default` which confused people. edge errors were like `ReferenceError: require is not defined`.

alex: yep. short summary we should add to docs: 1) provide both CJS and ESM snippets, 2) show how to import types in TS, 3) call out edge runtime constraints (no `require`, no Node built-ins).

pragya: example snippets help a lot. suggested copy for docs: CJS and ESM usage + minimal package.json markers.

alex: sample code (CJS):
```js
// Node <-> CommonJS
const { RedwoodClient } = require('@redwood/inference')
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })
```

alex: sample code (ESM):
```js
// package.json should set "type": "module" or use .mjs
import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood/inference'
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })
```

sam: for default vs named: if people do `const r = require('@redwood/inference')` and then try `new r()`, they hit `.default` wrapping when the package was compiled from ESM. quick workaround: `const { RedwoodClient } = require('@redwood/inference').default || require('@redwood/inference')` but that's messy. better to ship a CJS build that exports the same named symbols.

pragya: +1. also for TS: show `import type { RedwoodClientOptions } from '@redwood/inference'` and that types live in `dist/types`. some users on older TS configs couldn't find types because they were looking at `module` entry. docs should show where types resolve.

maria: edge runtime specifics? any small snippet for Cloudflare Workers or Vercel Edge?

alex: edge runtimes typically don't support `fs`, `child_process`, or `require`. we should provide a tiny ESM-only example that works in edge:
```js
// edge-friendly (Vercel/Cloudflare)
import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood/inference/esm' // or use package export `import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood/inference/edge'`
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: Deno.env?.REDWOOD_API_KEY || process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })
const res = await client.generate({ prompt: 'hi' })
```

sam: note: we don't actually publish an `/edge` entry yet. we can add a `exports` field in package.json to point to `./dist/esm/edge.js` and a top-level `dist/esm/index.js` for bundlers. that would make `import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood/inference'` pick the right build for ESM consumers.

pragya: also add a short troubleshooting section: common error for newbies: `TypeError: client.generate is not a function` — usually caused by importing default incorrectly. show the wrong + right examples.

maria: concrete action items I can take: 1) update onboarding docs with both snippets (CJS/ESM) + TS examples, 2) add an "Edge" note explaining constraints and a minimal example, 3) add link to sample app repo that uses ESM and Cloudflare worker. anyone want to volunteer a PR? :thumbsup:

alex: I'll open the docs PR. will include a small `examples/js/cjs`, `examples/js/esm`, and `examples/edge/worker` in the repo.

sam: I'll follow up and add a short compatibility matrix and a note about our package exports + where types live. also will add recommended Node versions and bundler hints (esbuild/webpack/rollup).

pragya: can someone add a one-liner in quickstart that prevents the most common mistake: explicitly show `import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood/inference'` and a footnote: "If you see `.default` after require, use the ESM import style or the CJS example."

maria: awesome — this should reduce onboarding friction. alex, sam: ping me when PRs are up and I'll coordinate a small announcement in #general and update the sample-app quickstart in the onboarding flow.

deploy-bot: docs-deploy queued for staging docs site — will publish once PRs land and CI passes.

maria: thanks all!
